headline: Military uses commercial 5G for drone defense in Latvia trials, powered by AI agents
summary: NATO's Digital Backbone Experimentation exercise in Latvia successfully tested using existing 5G masts to passively detect and track drones, with AI agents designing the system. A similar demo by AT&T and Ericsson in the US also showed promising results for lo
details: Militaries worldwide are exploring ways to leverage commercial 5G communications to enhance battlefield sensing and counter-drone capabilities. This approach aims to reuse existing infrastructure for drone detection, potentially offering a significant advantage in defense.

In Latvia, NATO recently conducted a Digital Backbone Experimentation exercise (DiBaX 2026) where 5G masts were used to passively detect and track flying objects, specifically drones. The trials, held between October 19 and 30, investigated whether existing large-scale telecommunications networks could serve a dual purpose, enhancing national security and gaining resilience.

The counter-drone engagement system tested by NATO was reportedly designed by AI agents. Admiral Pierre Vandier, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Transformation, noted that AI was used to connect disparate systems, overcoming interoperability barriers in hours.

Separately, in the U.S., AT&T and Ericsson demonstrated drone detection using advanced network sensing over a 5G network near a major sporting venue in Arlington, Texas. This system was capable of detecting, locating, and tracking multiple drones flying at altitudes between 300 and 400 feet within the coverage area, offering an early glimpse into 6G technology's sensing capabilities.

The potential advantage of this sensing technology is its ability to support new levels of low-altitude threat detection and tracking around major venues, public spaces, and other complex environments. With promising results from both experiments, leveraging commercial 5G and 6G for drone sensing networks appears to be a genuinely useful defense strategy with minimal additional investment required.
